items.description: Country of the employee's home address. It is also the employee's country of residence: it decides whether the employee lives abroad (and is therefore subject to source tax), which cross-border questions apply (Germany, Liechtenstein, other country), whether the canton is asked and whether the permit reminder is shown.

needed_by.purpose: Complete postal address for posting documents
Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax; the state of residence (Germany, Liechtenstein, other) drives the cross-border part of the tariff
Decides whether the canton is asked (only residents of Switzerland)

items.name: Canton
items.description: The Swiss canton for the pension fund's required 'Canton' field. Asked only from employees living in Switzerland (provisional, D-002).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland (home address country is Switzerland)

needed_by.purpose: Required 'Canton' field when registering the employee

items.notes: Step 2 'Home address'. What the fund expects for employees living abroad, and whether 'Canton' means residence or work, is open (OQ-canton-abroad).

items.name: First working day
items.description: The employee's first working day at Muster AG, entered and thereby confirmed by the employee (it often moves, e.g. after negotiating an earlier exit with the old employer). The pension fund insurance start date is derived from it.
items.asked_when: Always

needed_by.purpose: Basis for the insurance start date (the most important item for the registration)
Runs the onboarding around the start date; only HR can change it after submission

items.notes: Step 3 'Start of employment'. After submission only HR can change it; the latest date always counts and no history is kept (D-033). HR-side change is part of the later HR spec (D-034).

items.name: Nationality
items.description: The nationality of an employee living in Switzerland, needed to decide whether they are subject to source tax. Anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss, even with another nationality, and answers Switzerland.
items.form: Country by English name; employees holding Swiss citizenship answer "Switzerland"
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland

needed_by.purpose: Swiss citizens living in Switzerland are not subject to source tax
Non-Swiss employees get the reminder to bring their permit on the first day

items.notes: Step 4 'Nationality and permit'. Not asked from employees living abroad: they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality (D-038). See OQ-nationality-wording.

items.name: Holds a C permit (permanent residence)
items.description: Whether a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland holds a C permit (permanent residence). The permit type itself is not asked; only 'C permit or not' drives a rule.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland and is not Swiss

needed_by.purpose: Non-Swiss employees with a C permit are treated like Swiss people and are not subject to source tax

items.name: Civil status
items.description: The employee's civil status. Used for the pension fund (mapped to the fund's list) and for source tax (married/registered partnership vs. not married).
items.asked_when: Always

needed_by.purpose: Required 'Civil status' field (Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed); registered partnership and separated are entered as Married (provisional)
Married/registered partnership vs. single, divorced, separated, widowed decides the tariff letter, the spouse questions and the spouse exemption

items.notes: Step 5 'Civil status and spouse'. Fund mapping of registered partnership and separated is provisional (OQ-civil-status-partnership).

items.name: Spouse's / registered partner's date of birth
items.description: Date of birth of the employee's husband, wife or registered partner (for separated employees: of the spouse they are still married to).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee is married, in a registered partnership or separated (all entered at the fund as Married)

needed_by.purpose: 'Spouse's date of birth' is required when civil status is Married; registration is rejected without it

items.notes: Step 5. Not asked from divorced or widowed employees (OQ-spouse-dob-other-status, non-blocking).

items.name: Spouse's / partner's country of residence
items.description: The country where the employee's spouse or registered partner lives. Asked first among the spouse's source tax details, because a spouse living outside Switzerland can never exempt the employee, so nationality and permit are then not needed.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"]

needed_by.purpose: A Swiss or C-permit spouse exempts the employee only if the spouse lives in Switzerland

items.notes: Step 5. Asking residence before nationality and permit is an inference from data minimisation (G-01). Separated employees count as single for source tax (D-003), so they are not asked.

items.name: Spouse's / partner's nationality
items.description: Nationality of the spouse or registered partner living in Switzerland. A spouse with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss, even with another nationality.
items.form: Country by English name; a spouse holding Swiss citizenship is entered as "Switzerland"
items.asked_when: Only if the spouse/partner question block applies and the spouse lives in Switzerland
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"

needed_by.purpose: A Swiss spouse living in Switzerland exempts the employee from source tax

items.notes: Step 5. Applying the dual-citizenship rule (D-008) to the spouse is an inference (see OQ-nationality-wording).

items.name: Spouse / partner holds a C permit
items.description: Whether a non-Swiss spouse or registered partner living in Switzerland holds a C permit (permanent residence).
items.asked_when: Only if the spouse lives in Switzerland and is not Swiss (within the spouse block)
items.asked_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland" and spouse_nationality != "Switzerland"
items.required_when_expr: address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland" and spouse_nationality != "Switzerland"

needed_by.purpose: A spouse with a C permit living in Switzerland exempts the employee from source tax

items.required_when_expr: subject_to_source_tax and source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership"

items.name: Child lives in the same household
items.description: For each child: whether the child lives in the employee's household.

items.asked_when_expr: child_age_status in ["Minor", "Of age and in first education"]

items.name: Parental custody (child in household)
items.description: For a minor child in the household: whether custody is shared or sole.
items.asked_when: For a minor child living in the same household

needed_by.purpose: Sole custody counts the child (H for non-married employees)

items.name: Common household with the other parent
items.description: For the child: whether the employee lives in a common household with the child's other parent.
items.asked_when: For a minor child in the household with shared custody, or a child of age in first education living in the household
items.asked_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody") or (child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and child_same_household == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody") or (child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and child_same_household == "yes")

items.name: Shared custody (child not in household, married)
items.description: For married employees / registered partners with a minor child not living in the household: whether custody is shared.
items.asked_when: For a minor child not in the household, if the employee is married or in a registered partnership
items.asked_when_expr: source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Child count

items.name: Parental custody (child not in household, not married)
items.description: For non-married employees with a minor child not living in the household: whether the employee has parental custody.

items.asked_when_expr: source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"
items.required_when_expr: source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no"

needed_by.purpose: Child count and H tariff

items.name: Alternating care
items.description: For a minor child: whether the parents share care in alternation (alternating care).
items.asked_when: For a minor child in the household with shared custody and no common household with the other parent; or a minor child not in the household with shared custody (married) or parental custody (not married)
items.asked_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_shared_custody_not_in_household == "yes") or (source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_parental_care_not_in_household == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_parental_custody == "Shared custody" and child_common_household_other_parent == "no") or (source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_shared_custody_not_in_household == "yes") or (source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_parental_care_not_in_household == "yes")

items.description: Who makes the larger financial contribution to the child's maintenance: the employee or the other parent.

items.asked_when_expr: child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes")
items.required_when_expr: child_alternating_custody == "yes" or (source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_same_household == "yes" and child_common_household_other_parent == "yes")

needed_by.purpose: Child count and H tariff

items.notes: Step 7, per child. For married employees a common household with the other parent ends the child block without this question.

items.name: Child mainly maintained by the employee (more than 50%)

items.name: Daily return to the home in Germany
items.description: For employees living in Germany: whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany (subject to source tax)

needed_by.purpose: Decides whether the cross-border tariff applies

items.notes: Step 8 'Cross-border commuting' (Germany or Liechtenstein only). Asked after the children, as in the calculator.

items.name: Certificate of residence
items.description: For employees living in Germany who return daily: whether they have provided a certificate of residence (Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung). 'Not yet' is valid and counts as 'no' for the tariff code. The document goes to HR outside Lonio.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany and returns daily

needed_by.purpose: With a certificate the cross-border tariff applies
Knows whether a certificate is still outstanding

items.notes: Step 8. No upload in Lonio. A certificate handed in later is recorded by HR (D-037).

items.name: Daily return reasonable (less than 100 km)
items.description: For employees living in Germany who do not return daily: whether a daily return would in principle be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany and does not return daily

needed_by.purpose: Decides whether the cross-border tariff can apply

items.name: More than 60 work-related non-return days expected
items.description: For employees living in Germany for whom a daily return is reasonable but who do not return daily: whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year (a declaration, not proof).
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Germany, does not return daily and a daily return is reasonable

needed_by.purpose: More than 60 days gives the normal tariff, otherwise the cross-border tariff

items.name: Daily return to the home in Liechtenstein
items.description: For employees living in Liechtenstein: whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein.
items.asked_when: Only if the employee lives in Liechtenstein (subject to source tax)

needed_by.purpose: Daily return means in principle no source tax liability (subject to the double taxation agreement)

items.description: For employees living in Liechtenstein who do not return daily: whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the latest first working day: if it is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03. → 01.04.). It is always derived again when the first working day changes.

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status entered at the pension fund: Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed are taken as answered; registered partnership and separated are entered as Married (provisional).

rules.name: Civil status for source tax
rules.statement: For source tax, Married and Registered partnership count as 'Married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'Not married'.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(is_set(civil_status), "Not married", null))

rules.name: Spouse exempts from source tax
rules.statement: An employee who is married or in a registered partnership is exempt from source tax if the spouse/partner lives in Switzerland and is Swiss or holds a C permit.
rules.expression: source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland" and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_permit_type == "yes")

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is not subject if Swiss (including dual citizens) or holding a C permit, or if exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse/partner living in Switzerland; otherwise subject. Only subject employees get the source tax questions.
rules.expression: (is_set(address_country) and address_country != "Switzerland") or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and permit_type == "no" and not spouse_exempts_source_tax)

rules.name: State of residence for source tax
rules.statement: The calculator's residence answers are derived from the home address country: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein, or other country. Switzerland and other countries leave the base tariff unchanged.
rules.expression: if_else(address_country == "Switzerland", "Switzerland", if_else(address_country == "Germany", "Germany", if_else(address_country == "Liechtenstein", "Liechtenstein", if_else(is_set(address_country), "Other country", null))))

rules.name: Church-tax suffix
rules.statement: The tariff code ends in Y for Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed, and N for none or other.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.name: Base letter for married employees
rules.statement: For employees married or in a registered partnership: C if the spouse/partner is employed or receives replacement income, otherwise B.

rules.name: Child result (per child)
rules.statement: For each child the answers decide whether the child is not counted, counted, or (for non-married employees) counted with H, following the calculator's child logic. Rows marked inferred were not observed in the calculator and must be verified (OQ-calculator-coverage).
inputs: Parental custody (not in household, not married)

when: Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education

Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education
Of age and in first education

(child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee") or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and (child_alternating_custody == "no" or child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee")))) or (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_parental_care_not_in_household == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee") or (child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and ((child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee") or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_main_maintenance == "yes")))), "Counted with H", if_else((source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and child_same_household == "no" and child_main_maintenance == "yes") or (source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership" and ((child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "yes" and (child_parental_custody == "Sole custody" or child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee"))) or (child_age_status == "Minor" and child_same_household == "no" and child_shared_custody_not_in_household == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Employee") or (child_age_status == "Of age and in first education" and child_same_household == "yes" and (child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_main_maintenance == "yes"))) or rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose result is 'Counted' or 'Counted with H'; 0 without children. (The formal expression covers one child block; the digit is the sum over all children.)

table.then: Number of children counted (0 if none counts)

rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "no", 0, if_else(child_tariff_result in ["Counted", "Counted with H"], 1, if_else(child_tariff_result == "Not counted", 0, null)))

rules.name: H tariff for non-married employees
rules.statement: A non-married employee with at least one child counted with H gets an H tariff (e.g. A1 + H1 → H2N).
inputs: At least one child counted with H
rules.expression: source_tax_civil_status == "Not married" and child_tariff_result == "Counted with H"

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies
rules.statement: For employees living in Germany the cross-border tariff applies if they return daily and have provided a certificate of residence, or if they do not return daily, a daily return is reasonable and they do not expect more than 60 non-return days. 'Not yet' for the certificate counts as no. In all other cases the normal tariff applies.
rules.expression: address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: For employees living in Liechtenstein who return daily or expect at most 45 non-return days, the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code applies.

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: Base letter: C or B for married employees/registered partners (spouse employed or not); H for non-married employees with an H child; otherwise A. If the cross-border tariff applies, the letter is mapped A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P.
rules.expression: if_else(source_tax_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(married_tariff_letter == "C", if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "N", "C"), if_else(married_tariff_letter == "B", if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "M", "B"), null)), if_else(source_tax_civil_status == "Not married", if_else(single_parent_h_tariff, if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "P", "H"), if_else(cross_border_tariff_applies, "L", "A")), null))

rules.name: Source tax result
rules.statement: Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code for every employee subject to source tax: tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix (e.g. C1Y, L0Y, H2N). For Liechtenstein residents with daily return or at most 45 non-return days the result is 'In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. Employees not subject get no result. The result is always derived again from the latest answers.

table.then: Not subject to source tax (no tariff code)
In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement (flagged for HR)
Tariff code = tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix

rules.expression: if_else(subject_to_source_tax, if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle, "In principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", "Tariff code"), "Not subject to source tax")

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder, so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: If the employee changes an earlier answer so that later questions no longer apply, those answers may be kept while the employee goes back and forth, but are discarded on submission. After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee; later changes are made by HR.

open_questions.question: What should be entered in the pension fund's 'Canton' field for employees living abroad, and does 'Canton' mean canton of residence or of work?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The field is required and lists only Swiss cantons; employees abroad are not asked for it (D-002), so their registration may be blocked.
options: Fund provides another value or procedure for residents abroad
'Canton' means work canton for everyone – then ask nobody and use the work canton
open_questions.recommendation: Keep D-002 (ask only residents of Switzerland); a domain expert verifies with Pensionskasse Muster.

open_questions.question: How does Pensionskasse Muster want registered partnerships and separated employees registered (its list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed), and does it want the partner's details?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A wrong mapping gives the fund wrong civil status and possibly unnecessary or missing partner data.
options: Registered partnership → Married with partner's date of birth; Separated → Married (current provisional mapping)
Other mapping given by the fund
open_questions.recommendation: Keep the provisional mapping of D-003; verify with a domain expert and the fund.

open_questions.question: Does the fund's screen require the spouse's (or former spouse's) date of birth or other fields for Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The screenshots only show Single and Married; a hidden required field would block registration.
options: Extra field required – add a question
open_questions.recommendation: Domain expert obtains a screenshot of the fund screen for Divorced and Widowed.

open_questions.question: Does Lonio's computed tariff code match the Zurich calculator on the paths not explored: the residence block for A/B/H tariffs, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N, and the child rows marked inferred?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lonio now owns the tariff result; unverified paths could produce wrong tariff codes.
options: Domain expert compares computed codes with the calculator before go-live
open_questions.recommendation: Go-live condition per D-009; non-blocking for the spec.

open_questions.question: Should the questionnaire ask for the nationality as a country, or only whether the employee (and the spouse) holds Swiss citizenship? And does the dual-citizenship rule (D-008) also apply to the spouse?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only 'Swiss or not' drives a rule; asking the full nationality may collect more than needed (G-01). The spouse's dual citizenship is not covered by D-008.
options: Ask the nationality as a country, Swiss citizens answer Switzerland (current model)
Ask 'Do you hold Swiss citizenship? yes/no' only
open_questions.recommendation: Keep the current model and confirm with the product owner; apply D-008 to the spouse unless a domain expert says otherwise.
